judgments.rationale: In passage F002, the text states that the specified substitute refrigerants in the designated end-uses are exempt both 'from this prohibition' (the venting prohibition in paragraph (a)(1), captured in C0000) and 'from the requirements of this subpart' (which includes the practice and equipment mandates in paragraph (b), captured in C0004). Accordingly, qualifying both C0000 and C0004 as an exception is fully supported by the source.

Passage F013 establishes that de minimis releases are 'not subject to this prohibition', which solely targets the venting prohibition under paragraph (a)(1) (C0000). The text does not make de minimis releases an exemption to the separate violation rule for knowing release after recovery in paragraph (a)(3) (C0003), nor does it exempt parties from the affirmative practice and equipment requirements of paragraph (b) (C0004). In fact, observing those practices and using certified equipment is an express prerequisite under paragraph (a)(2)(i) for a release to qualify as de minimis. Qualifying C0003 and C0004 is therefore unsupported.

source_spans.quote:
(1) No person maintaining, servicing, repairing, or 
            
            disposing of an appliance or industrial process refrigeration may knowingly vent or otherwise release into the environment any refrigerant from such appliances. Notwithstanding any other provision of this subpart, the following substitutes in the following end-uses are exempt from this prohibition and from the requirements of this subpart:

(2) 
            De minimis
             releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerants are not subject to this prohibition. Except for exempt substitutes, refrigerant releases are 
            de minimis
             only if they occur when:

(i) The applicable practices in §§ 82.155 and 82.156 are observed, the applicable practices in § 82.157 are observed for appliances that contain any class I or class II refrigerant or blend containing a class I or class II refrigerant, recovery and/or recycling machines that meet the requirements in § 82.158 are used whenever refrigerant is removed from an appliance, the technician certification provisions in § 82.161 are observed, and the reclamation requirements in § 82.164 are observed; or

(ii) The requirements in subpart B of this part are observed.

(3) The knowing release of a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute refrigerant after its recovery from an appliance is a violation of the venting prohibition.

(b) No person may maintain, service, repair, or dispose of an appliance containing a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute refrigerant without:

(1) Observing the applicable practices in §§ 82.155, 82.156, and 82.157; and

(2) Using recovery and/or recycling equipment that is certified for that type of refrigerant and appliance under § 82.158.
